prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: On F.Cu the live conductor MAINS_L (0.80 mm track at x=40.500, y 19.010..40.990) runs parallel to the SELV net DHT22_DATA (0.30 mm track at x=39.600, y 34.120..37.120) with 0.900 mm centre-to-centre spacing = 0.350 mm of copper-to-copper air gap. Every other SELV item on that layer is also close: RELAY_CTRL 2.000 mm, RELAY_COIL_NEG 2.000 mm, pads D1.2/R1.2/R2.2 1.390 mm, unconnected pad J1.2 1.390 mm. The board DRC reports no clearance error, because MAINS_L sits in the power net class whose clearance is 0.30 mm.
expected: At 250 V RMS a mains-to-SELV gap on the same layer needs >=1.5 mm clearance for basic insulation and 3.0 mm clearance / 5.0 mm creepage for reinforced insulation (IEC 60664-1, pollution degree 2, material group IIIa) - the ~5 mm mains-to-SELV figure the rubric quotes. 0.350 mm fails basic by 1.15 mm and reinforced by roughly 4.65 mm.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (sections 1-3); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/clearance_report.txt; .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/my_drc_mains3p2.json (KiCad's own DRC at a 3.2 mm mains clearance: 14 mains violations)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The product declares a mains corridor rule area (keepout, B.Cu, rect x 39.0..52.0, y 5.72..44.72, copperpour not_allowed) to keep the ground pour clear of the mains run, but the corridor inner edge is only 1.100 mm from the live conductor's copper edge (mains copper edge x=40.100, pour resumes at x=39.000). The rule area is defined on B.Cu only, so the F.Cu SELV track at x=39.600 lies inside the corridor without violating it.
expected: A mains corridor on a board carrying mains should be at least the applicable clearance wide (>=3.2 mm basic at 250 V, ~5 mm reinforced) and the rule area must cover every layer on which mains and SELV share copper, otherwise it protects nothing.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 4); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/clearance_report.txt (MAINS_L vs B.Cu GND POUR = 1.100 mm for all three mains segments)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board carries no mains design rule of any kind. board_07.kicad_pro sets every board minimum to 0.0 (min_clearance, min_track_width, min_copper_edge_clearance, min_hole_clearance, min_hole_to_hole) and assigns MAINS_L to the same power net class as VCC_5V and GND with a 0.30 mm clearance. There is no stackup block in the .kicad_pcb, so no dielectric thickness is declared. The 0.350 mm mains gap of F-07-001 therefore passes the board's own rule with 0.05 mm to spare.
expected: A board that carries mains needs a named fab profile and rules that enforce mains clearance and creepage, checked against that fab's capabilities and not against tool defaults. A check before fab that has no mains rule cannot find a mains fault.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 7); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/board_07_copy.kicad_pro (pristine copy of the delivered project file)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The mains circuit is not a circuit. MAINS_L is the only mains net in the design. J1 pin 2 (the second terminal of the 2-pin mains connector, at 49.00,38.45) carries no net and has no copper attached; K1 pins 4 and 5 (the relay's other contact terminals, at 44.29,14.01 and 44.29,9.01) also carry no net and have no copper. There is no MAINS_N anywhere in board_ir.json. The relay's switched contact has nowhere to go and the mains connector's second leg is dead - the relay cannot switch mains and nothing on the board is a load.
expected: A relay that switches mains needs a mains input pair, the relay's switched contact wired to a load output, and a defined return. Every connection the design claims must have copper on the net.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 5); .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/clearance_report.txt (PADS WITH NO NET); board_07.kicad_pcb lines 154-169 (J1 pad 2 has no net) and 219-232 (K1 pads 4 and 5 have no net)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The two terminals of the mains connector J1 are 2.54 mm apart centre-to-centre, which is 1.040 mm of copper between them (pads 1.5 mm dia, r=0.75). J1.1 is the live MAINS_L conductor and J1.2 has no net; a user wiring the second terminal to neutral would put 1.040 mm between live and neutral.
expected: Two conductors of a mains circuit at the connector need at least the basic clearance for 250 V (>=1.5 mm), and more for reinforced isolation from the SELV side. 1.040 mm is below even the basic figure.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The board carries mains and has no fusing, no overcurrent protection, no mains marking and no creepage slot. The whole component list is U1, U2, K1, Q1, D1, R1, R2, C1, J1 - there is no fuse, no fuse holder and no series impedance in the mains path. The board also carries no MAINS or 250 VAC marking (see F-07-010), so nothing in the fab data identifies the live conductor to whoever wires it.
expected: A mains-switching board must be fused (at minimum, with a documented external fuse requirement), the live conductor must be identifiable on the board, and a slot or a stated spacing should separate the mains region from the SELV region. Nothing in the artifacts states any of this.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (sections 10 and 11); board_ir.json component list (9 components, no fuse)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The ground net exists only as a zone that was never filled. The delivered .kicad_pcb contains 0 occurrences of filled_polygon; a gerber exported from the delivered file has 0 region fills (G36) on B.Cu - only 52 pad/via flashes and 7 draws (the DHT22_DATA B.Cu track). As delivered there is no ground plane in the fab data and the GND pads are not connected: KiCad's DRC reports 4 unconnected items, all GND (U1.8, U1.22, U2.4, C1.2 and Q1.1 reported mutually unconnected). The product's drc.json and my independent kicad-cli run give the identical result.
expected: A board handed to a fab must arrive with its pours filled (or the fab flow must refill them) and with every net either routed in copper or connected by a filled plane. Four error-severity unconnected items is a board that will not work when assembled.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: K1's footprint does not match the part. CircuitOS:RELAY-SRD places the two pin rows 15.00 mm apart with 5.00 mm pitch (pad 1 at (-7.5,+5), pad 2 at (-7.5,-5), pads 3/4/5 at (+7.5,+5/0/-5)), i.e. a 15.00 x 10.00 mm pin rectangle inside a 20.0 x 16.0 mm courtyard. The SRD-05VDC-SL-C datasheet draws a 7.62 mm row-to-row spacing and a 7.62 x 10.16 mm pin rectangle in a 19.0 x 15.4 x 15.5 mm body. The body outline is right; the pin positions are roughly double the real spacing, so a real relay's pins cannot land on these pads.
expected: Each part's pins must land on pads matching the datasheet pin layout. A 15.00 mm row spacing against a 7.62 mm part means the relay is unbuildable, and the mains contact (K1 pin 3) is not where the fitted part's pin 3 is.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 8); board_07.kicad_pcb lines 170-233 (K1 footprint, pad offsets); board_ir.json K1 pads

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U2's DHT22 footprint has a courtyard of 8.20 x 15.60 mm (the four pads are on a correct 2.54 mm pitch in one row, and the pin assignment 1=VCC, 2=DATA, 3=NC, 4=GND is correct for the AOSONG DHT22), but the AOSONG DHT22 body is 25.1 x 15.1 x 8.1 mm. The body overhangs its own courtyard by about 17 mm. U2 is placed at x=10.12, so the sensor body either runs off the board edge (x<0) or reaches x=35.2 and overlaps U1 (courtyard x 14.81..25.83), Q1, D1, R1, R2 and K1.
expected: A footprint's courtyard must enclose the part's body, otherwise the placer can pack parts on top of each other and the assembly does not fit. Here the placement was computed on a body 8.2 mm wide when the part is 25.1 mm wide.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 9); board_ir.json U2 (courtyard_w 8.2, courtyard_h 15.6, x 10.12) and the U1/K1/Q1/D1/R1/R2 courtyards

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: There is no silkscreen at all. The .kicad_pcb contains exactly one occurrence of F.SilkS - the layer declaration - and no fp_text or fp_line on that layer; the exported F_Silkscreen.gto contains 0 draw/flash objects. The reference designators (C1, D1, J1, K1, Q1, R1, R2, U1, U2) exist only on F.Fab, which is not an assembly layer.
expected: A board going to fab and assembly needs silkscreen reference designators, a pin-1 mark on the DIP-28, a cathode band on D1, a pin-1 mark on the DHT22 and the relay, polarity marks, and mains markings. Without them the board cannot be populated or inspected from the fab data, and D1's cathode and U1's pin 1 are undecidable.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: There is no decoupling capacitor on the microcontroller. U1 pin 7 (VCC) and pin 8 (GND) have no capacitor at all, and there is no bulk capacitance for the relay coil. The single capacitor C1 (100 nF, value code 104) is 6.84 mm from the DHT22's own supply pad, on the far side of the sensor, and nothing decouples the relay coil current from the 5 V rail.
expected: A 100 nF ceramic at the ATmega328P VCC/GND pins within a few mm, local decoupling at the DHT22, and a bulk cap for the relay coil are standard practice - and mandatory on a board that switches a relay next to a microcontroller.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 12); board_ir.json (C1 is the only capacitor; none on U1.7/U1.8); clearance_report.txt pad list

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The request was for an Arduino Uno on the same board as the relay and the DHT22. The board contains a bare ATMEGA328P-PU in a DIP-28 footprint and no Uno whatsoever: no 5 V regulator, no power input connector, no USB, no ICSP, no 16 MHz crystal (U1 pins 9 and 10 are unconnected), no reset circuit and no Arduino headers. The only connector on the board is the 2-pin mains terminal J1, whose second leg has no net, and VCC_5V has no source anywhere on the board. The MCU pin choices are otherwise Uno-consistent (U1.4 = PD2 / D2 to DHT22_DATA, U1.5 = PD3 / D3 to the relay base).
expected: Either the board is the Uno - and then it needs the Uno's power, clock, reset and programming - or it is a shield for an Uno - and then it needs headers to plug into one. As laid out it can be neither: it cannot be powered, programmed, or connected to the Arduino Uno named in the request.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 11); board_ir.json component list and U1 pad nets; clearance_report.txt (PADS WITH NO NET - U1.9, U1.10 open)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: U1 pin 21 (AVCC, the analog supply of the ATmega328P) has no net and no copper attached. U1 pin 20 (AREF) is tied directly to the VCC_5V rail with no filter, and U1 pin 22 (ADC6) is strapped to GND.
expected: AVCC is the supply for the ADC comparator and must be connected to VCC, directly or through a filter. AREF should be tied to AVCC through 100 nF or a ferrite, or left unconnected, not wired straight to the 5 V rail. This board leaves the analog supply floating.

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The mains conductor is a 0.80 mm track on 1.6 mm FR4 with 35 um copper: about 1.6-1.9 A at a 10 C rise by the IPC-2152 external-conductor table, while the relay fitted (SRD-05VDC-SL-C) is a 10 A device. The mains connector pads are 1.5 mm with a 1.0 mm drill. Nowhere in board_ir.json, the board file or the DRC report is the switched load current stated, so nothing establishes that the conductor is rated for the load it is meant to carry.
expected: The switched current must be stated, and the conductor, the connector pads and the relay contact sized for it against a stated rise-temperature budget. A mains board whose current is never stated cannot be released to a fab.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 1 for the 0.8 mm width); board_ir.json layers (1.6 mm board, 35 um copper) and net_classes (MAINS_L track_width 0.8)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: The product's own report of the check it ran on this board reports no errors. drc_summary.json says violations 9, unconnected_items 4, by_type {lib_footprint_issues: 9}, severity_error_violations 0, while the drc.json it points at lists those same 4 unconnected items each with severity error. My independent kicad-cli 10.0.1 run on the delivered board gives the identical verdict (9 violations, 4 unconnected items). The summary therefore reports 0 error violations for a board whose own DRC contains four connectivity errors, and says nothing at all about clearance, creepage, fusing, current or the unfilled ground plane.
expected: A verification summary must carry the errors it found, with their severity, and must state which checks were not performed. Reporting a board with four error-severity unconnected items as having zero error violations is a false pass on the connectivity class.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 13); drc_summary.json vs drc.json in artifacts/board_07; .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/my_drc.json (independent run, same result)

prompt: An Arduino Uno drives a relay whose contact switches mains, and reads a DHT22 sensor on the same board. Lay the board out and check it before you would send it to a fab.
observed: D1 (1N4007, DO-41) has pad 1 = VCC_5V and pad 2 = RELAY_COIL_NEG, i.e. across the relay coil. Under the KiCad convention (Device:D pin 1 = cathode) that is the correct polarity for a flyback diode - cathode to +5 V, anode to the collector. But the CircuitOS footprint library is not shipped with the board and the footprint has no cathode band, so the polarity cannot be confirmed from the fab data; if the product's library maps pin 1 to the anode, D1 is a short across the 5 V rail through Q1.
expected: The fab data must make each polarised part's orientation unambiguous - a cathode band on the silkscreen, or a documented library mapping included with the board.
evidence: .claude/shared-memory/alpha/runs/evidence_board_07/mains_clearance_evidence.txt (section 12); board_07.kicad_pcb lines 112-127 (D1 pad nets); drc.json lib_footprint_issues for D1 (library not present in the configuration)
